claim: At score >= 5, the known nuclear transients pass more often than objects in the Unknown stratum.
rationale: Same threshold and primary stratum as the earlier run recorded in missions/ztf-nuclear-transients/README.md, applied to a new sample of weeks. Unknown is the bulk of the real alert stream, so it is the background that matters most for inspection load.
failure_interpretation: On this sample the screen does not separate the known objects from the Unknown stratum. I will not change the threshold, the primary stratum, the seed or the objects to recover the claim.
alternative_explanations: Circularity: the known objects were selected by a TDE classifier and by eye for looking like this, and the threshold of 5 was chosen after their scores had been seen. The positive side is the same objects in every run and is not independently replicated here; this run repeats the background side.
Chance: about 12 background objects per class and 19 positives make the intervals wide.

Sampling: a stratum is drawn from the last 3000 alerts of its class in the sampled week, so a busy class such as Unknown covers only the tail of one night and objects that alert often are over-represented.
Observation effort: detection counts and duration depend on how often a field was observed, not only on the object.
seen_before_lock: The mission README, including the earlier run's table at score >= 5 and its stated known limits. The demo output on synthetic light curves. The plan (not data) of contributions/2026-11-23-first, which uses seed 2207. No data of this run.
ai_budget: About 25 minutes of agent work; a small run is fine. Stop after ultra export.
